source.title: Competency-based education for CBSE — Item Bank: Maths Class 7 (September 2021)
source.subject: mathematics
source.authorityName: Central Board of Secondary Education (content created by the British Council)
source.usage: Official CBSE item bank, freely available on cbseacademic.nic.in for teachers to use as they wish; question text reproduced for study with attribution and a link to the original. Figures are not reproduced.
source.notes: A bank of practice items published by CBSE (content created by the British Council, September 2021), not an examination paper. Each item is identified by its printed item identity (e.g. Maths7KG5), used here as 'number'; every item's question is printed as '1', so sub-parts use part '(a)', '(b)', '(c)'. Answers come from the mark scheme printed after each item in the same document. The items were written for the NCERT books current in 2021; chapters were mapped to the current Ganita Prakash (Grade 7) syllabus by topic and must be confirmed. Topics with no matching current Class 7 chapter (percentages, simple interest, ratio/proportion, exponents, perimeter/area, 3-D shapes, Pythagoras theorem) have chapter null. Several printed mark-scheme answers look inconsistent with their own guidance; they are reproduced as printed and flagged. Math italic Unicode letters in the text layer were normalised to plain letters; flattened powers/fractions were rebuilt only where unambiguous and flagged.

Degree signs in the official answer flattened in extraction ('300 or 600'); rebuilt as 30° or 60°

officialAnswer.text: CB = 6cm. ∆ACB ≅ ∆ACD. Using RHS (Right Angle-Hypotenuse-Side) rule. Or: one of the angles in ABC is 30° or 60° because then the triangles are similar (same angles) with a common side (so congruent). Guidance: M1: Use of RHS to prove congruency OR Indication that the triangles share a hypotenuse; A1 ∠ABC = ∠ADC = Right angle; AC = AC (As both the triangles share the same hypotenuse); Therefore, if CB = 6 cm = CD Then ∆ACB ≅ ∆ACD Using RHS (Right Angle-Hypotenuse-Side) rule. Allow alternative congruency conditions with the correct additional value given.

questions.text: Anuj and Urvashi invested Rs 8,000 in a simple interest scheme. After 10 years, Anuj had an amount of Rs 18,000. Calculate the total interest Anuj received

officialAnswer.text: Rs 10,000. M1 Interest = Amount – Principal; Interest = Rs 18,000 – Rs 8,000 = Rs 10,000. Allow 1 mark only for correct answer.

questions.text: Anuj and Urvashi invested Rs 8,000 in a simple interest scheme. After 10 years, Anuj had an amount of Rs 18,000. After 6 years, Urvashi had earned Rs 6,000 interest. Find out the interest rate percent per annum. Show your working.

officialAnswer.text: 12.5 %. M1 6,000 = (8,000 × Rate of interest × 6) / 100 OR Rs 1000 interest per year; Rate = 10% x 1000/8000 OR equivalent; A1 Rate of interest = 12.5 (%). Answer only 1 mark
